about.title: The City of Seven Lakes
paragraphs: Known as the City of Seven Lakes, San Pablo is a 1st class component city in Laguna with a strong identity shaped by nature, heritage, and community.
Founded as San Pablo de los Montes and chartered as a city in 1940, it continues to grow as a center for public service, tourism, and local enterprise.

history.title: A City Shaped by Time
history.subtitle: Important milestones that shaped San Pablo City — from its earliest settlement to modern civic life.

items.title: Parish Founding
items.description: San Pablo de los Montes was established as a parish, forming the religious and civic foundation of the city.

items.title: Elevated to Municipality
items.description: The settlement was formally elevated to a municipality, beginning centuries of local governance.

items.title: City Charter Approved
items.description: Commonwealth Act No. 520 was signed on May 7, 1940, granting San Pablo its city charter — one of the oldest cities in the Philippines.

items.title: City Inauguration
items.description: San Pablo City was inaugurated on March 30, 1941, marking the formal start of city governance.

items.title: Diocese of San Pablo Established
items.description: The Roman Catholic Diocese of San Pablo was established on November 28, 1967, with the Cathedral of St. Paul the First Hermit as its seat.

items.title: First Coconut Festival
items.description: The Coco Festival was launched to celebrate the 400th anniversary of the parish and to promote the city's coconut heritage and local industry.

items.title: City Central Terminal Opened
items.description: The San Pablo City Central Terminal was inaugurated, modernizing public transport and improving connectivity for residents.

items.title: New Administration Begins
items.description: Arcadio "Najie" B. Gapangada Jr. was elected City Mayor with 70,822 votes, beginning a new chapter for San Pablo City governance.

festival.title: Coco Festival of San Pablo
festival.description: Held every January 9–15, the Coco Festival culminates on January 15 — the Feast Day of St. Paul the First Hermit, the city's patron saint. First held in 1996, it is a DOT and ATOP award-winning tourism event.
highlights: Street dancing competition with elaborate coconut-themed costumes and floats.
Mutya at Lakan ng San Pablo — the city's signature beauty pageant.
Coco Trade Fair showcasing coconut farmers, MSMEs, and local products.
Recognized as a Guinness World Record event for mass coconut planting in 2025.
